utterances.text: On the evening of the 11th, that they would check this out. That's what he told the representatives of UNPROFOR and the representatives of the Muslim people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What did he say, did General Mladic say?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mladic said that the members of the 28th Division must be checked out in order to find people who had perhaps committed war crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you discuss this with the command staff on the 11th of July or the 12th of July, how this would be done?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at all, because that was not my task, or any task in connection to this, and anything else when it came to the civilian population and the members of the 28th Division. I was given no assignment of any kind in that regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Could I just clarify one thing, General? You said that General Mladic said that members of the 28th Division must be checked out to see if they had committed war crimes. When you say "members of the 28th Division," in your memory, if that was the term that General Mladic used, is that the same as any man of military age who might be found in Potocari? I mean, when you say "members of the 28th Division would be checked out," did you understand that to mean any man of military age that might be found in Potocari? In other words, was he drawing a distinction between members of the 28th Division, who would be army people, and civilian men, or was, in your view, he was equating any man of military age who might be found in Potocari among the refugees would be included in this screening to see if they had committed war crimes?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as regards any special details in his speech, they did not exist, but I understood that he wanted to screen the members of the 28th Division, regardless of where they were located, where they were to be found.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Did you understand that to mean that if there were men of military age among the refugees in Potocari, they would be screened out, they would be screened to see if they had committed war crimes?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was obvious from his -- from what he said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. McCloskey, I apologise for interrupting as well, but I would like to ask the following. General, you said that you were somewhat concerned with respect to seeing how the civilian people at the meeting were going to do something to disarm the 28th. Is my understanding correct?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You said on several occasions, as somebody who knew General Mladic well, that he gave the choice either to survive or to disappear. Were you not preoccupied with the fate of those civilians, what was to become of them?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said earlier on that nobody could or dared comment on anything that General Mladic said. It was a fait accompli. And my thoughts were thoughts that remained deep inside me. They were my own personal thoughts. I wondered how the representatives, that is to say, those two people who were present at the meeting, would be able to implement what General Mladic was requesting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And with respect to your thoughts and deliberations, were you deeply concerned or was this just a superficial thought: Well, they'll get by it somehow; they'll find a way out somehow? What was the degree of your preoccupations? What did you feel at this time? To what degree did you feel this or give it thought?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought that the representatives of the Muslim people and the UNPROFOR command would contact the 28th Division and that they would find a solution of some kind. Those were my thoughts, along those lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Very well. Thank you. Mr. McCloskey, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: General Krstic, in Exhibit 271, the Srebrenica missing document, there are approximately 1.400, mostly men, that are reported missing by their relatives on 12 and 13 July in Potocari. Based on your experience, having been there, does that seem about right to you, 1.400 men of military age in Potocari at the time?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have that exhibit in front of me, and I cannot make any assessment as to whether that figure is a correct one. I said earlier on that all my knowledge about those events, because at noon on the 12th I had already left the area, so that all my knowledge came much later.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: In the reviewing of prisoners for war crimes, would it be normal to take their identification documents away from them and discard them?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw that here during the proceedings. I don't know who did that nor for what purpose. I am still not certain whether those documents were there, but clearly, from what I saw, there were some such instances as well. The normal procedure would be to establish the identity of those people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So if their identity and their other personal property was taken from them and destroyed, like we saw, that would not be a normal part of an investigation into war crimes?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It is the submission of the Prosecution that the plan to separate the military-aged men at Potocari was developed sometime prior to the actual separation of those men from their families and removal of their documents. Can you comment on this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Petrusic. I think perhaps we have all seen the same thing. The Prosecutor -- your formulation of the question was: "That would not be a normal part of an investigation into war crimes." Is that a statement or a question? The answer was "No." So we have to conclude. Was it normal or not normal? In any event, that is what I noticed. But Mr. Petrusic has something to say too.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As it has to do with the English translation, Mr. Visnjic will do it better than I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we've just lost the line that I wanted to comment on, because the Prosecutor said that from Exhibit 271, it appears that 1.400 men disappeared in Potocari, and that line has disappeared from the screen, but I found that document, and in that document, maybe the translation is wrong, but no number of missing people from Potocari is mentioned in that document. So that would be my observation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Mr. McCloskey, you have at least two points to react to and clarify. The mentioned document, does it indeed give this number? It's not so important for the question, but if the number figure is in the record, perhaps we need to clear it up. The other thing is whether it was normal or not to remove the documents of persons that were being screened.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. On point one, you have to count in the document to come up with that number, and the persons that have been helping us with these documents have done that and came up with the number above 1.400. So I was just using that as a gauge to see if the General could help me estimate. This can be done because the document lists missing in Potocari and the dates. And on point two, you're absolutely correct. That question could have been framed differently, and I think I can clear that up very quickly. I'm sure that the General will agree with me that this was not the normal procedure, to take ID documents and destroy them in part of any investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Is that right, General? This would not be a normal thing to do?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It would not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is that clear now, Mr. Visnjic? We are not discussing now the number of missing persons. The question put to the General was to see whether it was normal to have such a large number of people. Whether it is 1.000 or 1.400, I don't think that is relevant. Mr. Visnjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am satisfied with Mr. McCloskey's explanation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. McCloskey, continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's the submission of the Prosecution that the plans to murder the military-aged men from Potocari began -- was developed prior to their separation at Potocari. Can you comment on this?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of any plan nor of any indications or signs that anything like that could happen. The Drina Corps Command was not contemplating entering Srebrenica even, never mind having a plan of this kind or of knowing of such a plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we go now to Exhibit 445A, and if the General could be given the B/C/S version. It is an intercept dated 12 July, 12.50 hours, between General Mladic and an unidentified male person.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Take a moment to look at that. And I would call your attention to, in particular, in the middle of the page where, according to this document, General Mladic says, "They've all capitulated and surrendered and we'll evacuate them all - those who want to and those who don't want to." And the person responds and says, "I understand, General." Now, based on your knowledge now as you sit in this courtroom, do you believe the Muslim refugees had a free choice whether to go to the Muslim territory or whether to stay in the former enclave?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what kind of choice they had, but at the meeting in Bratunac on the 12th, they decided to go to the territory under the control of the authorities of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you believe this was under their own free will, without coercion?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not able to comment on that, because they decided to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you know whether or not the people at the meetings, Muslim people, were afraid? Could you see their fear at those meetings?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't notice anything more in relation to what I have already said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could address the General again to Exhibit 399A bis, and that is the transcript of the open version of his interview with Mr. Ruez. He should have a highlighted section marked on page 20 of the B/C/S version, and if we could put page 33 of the English version on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE USHER
utterances.text: Which page in the English?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The English is page 33, and it's page 20 in the B/C/S -- version of the B/C/S. General, if you could go to that page 20, and it starts, "As far as the deportation is concerned ..." which is the second paragraph. If you could zero in the ELMO on that, the second -- well -- there you go. That's it. That's fine. And I'll just read part of this: "As far as the deportation is concerned, since that is the first activity on the list, and this is what I have information on, this is what happened: The deportation took place on the 12th and 13th of July. This was organised, led, and managed by the Commander of the Main Staff, through these senior officers that I have listed. General Mladic was the one who was literally there, commanding the loading of people onto buses."

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you stand by that statement, General?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That could be seen during the proceedings. Yes. I said, "Yes."

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And you were also there on 12 July, in the afternoon, in Potocari, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stayed at the checkpoint, from which I went back and then I continued along Bratunac, Voljevica, Sase, Pribicevac. I had absolutely no contact with civilians or with UNPROFOR members. I was there for a very brief spell of time at the checkpoint, and I intended to go through Srebrenica, and that is what I said in the course of my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. We'll get into that a little more later, hopefully soon. But if we could now go to Exhibit 446A, which is an intercept at 1305 hours in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: General, do you recall where you might have been -- or excuse me -- where you were at about 1300 hours?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At 1300 hours, I was on the way -- on the road between Voljevica, Sase, and Pribicevac. That was the time when I went back from the checkpoint at Potocari, heading towards the forward command post at Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you have the ability to communicate over radio or telephone during your transportation period that you've just described?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There's no telephone along the road. And even when I reached Pribicevac -- this was about 1400 hours -- there were no lines, because the communication centre had been dismantled in the night between the 11th and the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Looking at this Exhibit 446, do you know of a Drina Corps person named Sobot?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was an officer in the logistics body of the Drina Corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And I note further down there's mention of the Vlasenica Brigade, which, of course, was a Drina Corps Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Then there's mention of a Kosoric, and there was a Lieutenant Colonel Kosoric that was the Chief of Intelligence for the Drina Corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kosoric was a Chief of Intelligence in the Corps Command, and there is another Lieutenant Colonel Kosoric, the Commander of the Vlasenica Brigade. At the time, he was a Major.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So in the context of this conversation, this "Give me Kosoric" would more likely be the Kosoric that's the chief of the Vlasenica Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who was asking for him. There are two Kosorics.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, there's a mention -- it says, "Give me Savo. Put me through to Savo." And do you know anyone in the logistics area of the Vlasenica Brigade that has a first name or a nickname of Savo?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was an officer by the name of Savo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what was his full name?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember his surname now, but his name is Savo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Is it Captain Celikovic?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possible. There were quite a number of Celikovics. There were other Celikovic officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did he have a nickname Srpski or is that just a general exclamation about a fellow Serb?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he had any kind of nickname.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Is there a tunnel near the drop-off point at Luke school where refugees were dropped off to walk toward the Muslim territory?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there is a tunnel going from Tisca towards Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. If we could go back to the interview page. It's the Exhibit 399, same page, just a little bit farther down. Page 33 on the English version, page 20 on the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: General, you have now testified that you recall going in the area of Potocari on 12 July, and I want to read some of the things that you mentioned to Mr. Ruez in your interview and ask you about that. I would start at line 20 of the English version. "I do declare that not a single soldier of the Drina Corps came to the area of Potocari, nor would General Mladic have allowed that, except for those people of his.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: There was no Drina Corps soldier present in Potocari; is that clear?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Only the 65 Protection Regiment soldiers and maybe the 10th Sabotage Detachment as well?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These were the officers and soldiers from the battalion of the military police," and you go on to explain them. So on the 12 July, we understand that you've said that you were there, Popovic was there, Kosoric was there in the photos. Were there any other Drina Corps soldiers or officers present in Potocari on 12 July, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I stopped at the checkpoint only. I didn't pass through Potocari. With the exception of Lieutenant Colonel Kosoric, who started off with me to go to the Pribicevac forward command post, I don't know on whose assignment Lieutenant Colonel Popovic arrived. The other officer at the checkpoint from which I returned -- I didn't see any other officers. At the checkpoint, I only saw soldiers that I didn't know who were wearing better camouflage uniforms than those worn by soldiers of the Drina Corps, and it was on that basis that I said this to Mr. Ruez.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could now go to page 27 on the -- excuse me, page 46 on the English version and page 27-28 on the B/C/S version of the interview. I'll start at just a few lines from the question at line 9. "Q. Did you have any opportunity, on a personal level, to go and check on your own the refugee situation in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, no. The way I went to Viogora was Bratunac. It's an old mine. Sase, Pribicevac, Zeleni Jadar, and Viogora.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So you never went into Potocari itself to have a look at the situation of the people there, if men were still among them?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no, absolutely not. One could not have passed after the arrival of General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: May I ask, then, how can you be so sure that these separations in Potocari were conducted by the 65th Protection Regiment members, and maybe other of these Main Staff units and not by, let's say, the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Bratunac Brigade wasn't even there; wasn't even in the area." Next page: "On the 11th of July, the Bratunac Brigade could not have got to the area where the refugees were. A Military Police Battalion of the 65th Regiment, on the 11th of July, in the evening, had already blocked Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So you are certain and straight on the fact that no Bratunac Brigade members had anything to do in Potocari during the 12th of July and the 13th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you already that those units that were under command of the brigade commanders were certainly not deployed in the area in this way. However, it may have happened that individuals were appointed by General Mladic and Colonel Beara." Okay. First I want to ask you, when you tell Mr. Ruez, on the previous page, that you did not check in on the situation in Potocari, has your recollection been refreshed as a result of the material you've seen, or do you consider this answer meaning that you did not get into Potocari?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I continue to claim that I did not go to Potocari. I only went as far as the checkpoint in Potocari. I was there briefly. I granted an interview there and then I went back and headed towards Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Where was that checkpoint in relation to the UN base?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember now exactly where that checkpoint was. I'm not familiar enough with Potocari nor did I have time to make any visits, not only Potocari, but many other places in the responsibility of the corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How far were --

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't learn anything in particular that would have impressed itself on my mind so that I would remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How far were you from the area where the refugees were being blocked and assembled in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see a single refugee. That can clearly be seen on the shot when I was giving the interview. I didn't see a single refugee. And that is why I cannot remember where it was exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you have knowledge of members of the Bratunac Brigade being in Potocari on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw and heard this from witnesses during the proceedings, when some were named individually, and I saw someone who is identified here as -- I think his name was Kovacevic. Until then, I had no knowledge as to the presence of the Bratunac Brigade in the Potocari area, either individuals or units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How about other members of the Drina Corps? Do you have knowledge of other members of the Drina Corps that we haven't mentioned already being in Potocari on 12 July or 13 July?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no knowledge about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And when you stopped the vehicle and got out of the vehicle to give the press interview, as you've described, how far did you walk from your vehicle to give the interview?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I didn't walk anywhere because I moved with great difficulty anyway. So I couldn't walk around or spend any length of time there. I stayed there only for as long as the interview lasted, and then I got back into my car and turned back.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I believe it's a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We're going to have a 15-minute break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. McCloskey, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If we could proceed with the playing of Exhibit 66, which is the very brief video of the interview. And prior to playing it, perhaps we should get the transcript, which is Exhibit 67, of that brief interview. If we could play the video. And yes, if you could put the transcript on the ELMO. It's just a one-pager, and General Krstic has the B/C/S of the transcript. But, obviously, could we play the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we stop? I'm sorry. This video worked the first time. Is there any way to make it work? This obviously was not working. Can we give it one more try and then we'll go on.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The video booth has informed me that they're working on it, so it should take a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps, Mr. McCloskey, if you have another question. No, we have it. We seem to have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I can ask a couple as we wait.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: General Krstic, who was in the vehicle with you that stopped at this checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My driver, Dalibor Krstic, and the driver Vlado Tosic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Earlier you mentioned Lieutenant Colonel Kosoric. Was he with you in this area of Potocari?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had his own vehicle and he went with me to pass through Srebrenica to go to Pribicevac, because throughout that time he was at Pribicevac with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So he was stopped at the same place you were in Potocari, Colonel Kosoric?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And who was with Lieutenant Colonel Kosoric?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who was in the car with him, but we saw from the video that behind us was Lieutenant Colonel Popovic. He was standing behind us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So do you think Lieutenant Colonel Popovic was travelling in the same vehicle as Lieutenant Colonel Kosoric?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. Each of them had their own vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What other vehicles were in your group of vehicles, yours and Kosoric's, that got stopped at the same time, if any?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was my vehicle, and behind me was Lieutenant Colonel Kosoric. I didn't see Lieutenant Colonel Popovic come there at all. I didn't see him arrive.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Were there only two vehicles, then, in your group that were stopped?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just my vehicle and the vehicle of Lieutenant Colonel Kosoric. I don't know where the vehicle belonging to Lieutenant Colonel Popovic was, whether it went behind us at all or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How are we on the video?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: There seems to be a problem with the video, so they're trying to correct it. The video is still jumping, but the sound is okay. That's the best that they could do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, let's pass on the jumpy video and perhaps try that tomorrow. And we have a still, Exhibit 58, that we can go with for now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, General Krstic, can you identify the faces, if you can, in this video? Let's start with the person who's immediately behind you, over your right shoulder. Do you know who that person is?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's my driver, Dalibor Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I know we don't really get a very good view of the person over your left shoulder. Do you have any recollection or do you know his nose well enough to make an ID?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And the person farther back. I know this is a blurry picture, but we've seen this video. Is that Lieutenant Colonel Popovic?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's quite far off, but the appearance does seem to indicate that it is Lieutenant Colonel Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And in the video, we notice trucks going by you during the interview, in both directions, I believe. What were the purposes of those big trucks?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you know at the time?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't pay attention to that at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And in the -- and referring to number 67, the transcript of your interview, you talk about the Drina Corps carrying out this operation very successfully. "We did not halt the operation. We'll go all the way to liberate Srebrenica territory. We guarantee the security of the civilian population." So you were making a guarantee, over Serb video, of the civilian population; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just said what General Mladic said to those who attended the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: When you said "we guarantee," who did you mean?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said. What General Mladic said, I conveyed that; same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Meaning "We, the VRS"?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you do anything yourself to guarantee the security of the civilian population at the time, either before you made this statement or afterward?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't -- wasn't given that assignment at all. I was given my assignment from General Mladic, and that assignment was Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: There were also buses in the video. Do you know what the buses were for?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't notice any buses. Perhaps they -- it is quite possible that they passed by or that they arrived at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What time was this, as best you can recall?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the meeting ended. The meeting ended at about 12.00, so it could have been about 1230 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, if we could go to Exhibit number 184.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Excuse me. The meeting of the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: General, we have, we see, Lieutenant Colonel Kosoric in the back of a -- and we'll show the still of that -- but we see him in the back of the film of the interview with a Bratunac Brigade officer, and since he was -- Kosoric was within your party, do you know, in relation to time, when this Bratunac officer gave the interview that Kosoric is in the back of?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did Lieutenant Colonel Kosoric travel down to wherever you were going when you left this area with you?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I ordered him to report to me at Krivaca on the 13th at the forward command post, and he was there. He did not continue on with me to Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Getting back to the exhibit that's there, now, this is a photograph not taken at the time of the events. Mr. Ruez testified that this is based on his study of the video. This is the general area where he felt you were standing. Now, I don't know if you can make anything out of this photograph or not, but can you tell us, does this photograph help you in identifying whether or not you were standing between these two arrows that Mr. Ruez has identified?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't say. I'm not able to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you see this blue tinted building in the background behind the two vehicles, with a power pole sticking up behind it? Do you recall that building at all?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't pay attention to the buildings, and I can't remember whether that is that building or some other one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could go to Exhibit 769, which is a blow-up of an aerial. And if we could put it on the easel, that would be helpful. It's right here in front of me. Yes, easel first. And if you could place that so the General can get a good look at it, pointing in his direction. And if the camera could zero in on the area around the red arrows. Now, General, on this exhibit, this is a 12 July aerial photograph from the United States, around 1400 hours. And for the record, Mr. Ruez has recently marked with two red arrows the area that his analysis has determined General Krstic to have been in. And for the record --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And General Krstic, down in the very right-hand corner of that photograph, you can see what's been marked as an X. That is the part of the UN compound, and the entrance of the UN compound is unfortunately off the photograph, but that is the area of the UN compound, just off the photograph to the south, what would be the south or below the photograph. Now, using buses for a scale, by this photograph you're four or five bus lengths from the crowd of people during this interview. Do you have any reason to dispute this as the location where you gave the interview?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know Potocari that well, so I cannot claim that I was there at that spot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have an objection to make to the form in which the question was asked. When he said that it was four or five bus lengths away, as far as I can see the photograph, I don't think that is a good way of putting it. Perhaps the question could be reformulated. But from my angle of vision, I couldn't say, and therefore I think that the question ought to be reformulated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I can try to be as clear as possible on this point, but we have the bus yard, the express bus compound in the centre of this photograph, and I think we can see very clearly three buses adjacent to the crowd of people. And on these kind of photographs, a very simple scale is always the best way to go, and I was just using what appears to be buses -- there has been testimony of witnesses that stayed in buses in this area -- as a means to gauge distance. If the witness disagrees, fine, but I was just trying to simplify it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But you started saying that you were going to be more precise in your questions, so that's what we're asking for. Please try to be more precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: General Krstic, had you been some 150 -- sorry, Your Honour. I was using feet. Did you see any people during your interview on the television in the vicinity of where that crowd of people is gathered?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One civilian -- I didn't see a single civilian refugee there. I stopped there for a very brief period of time, after which I returned. I didn't even try to notice everything. I was in a hurry. I was on my way to the former -- to the forward command post of Pribicevac, and I've already said that it was my intention to pass through Potocari and to go through Srebrenica to go to Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Were you able to --

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why should I contest that? Why should I contest passing through Potocari? I am speaking the truth, that I came there, I was stopped, I gave the interview, I didn't even know that I was going to give it, and then I returned to the forward command post. I took the direction that I spoke about earlier on. I'm not afraid of anything. I'm not afraid of saying that I passed through Potocari if I passed through Potocari, but I did not pass through Potocari. I just stayed there for a very brief period of time. And the statements that I was there on the 12th and the 13th, that really is -- well, it's something that's quite unprecedented.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Are you contesting Mr. Ruez's location of you between these two arrows on --

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I don't know Potocari, especially as this is an aerial photograph, not even on this photograph here, the building. I didn't notice anything out of -- anything that I would remember, that would have stayed in my mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The white house that has been shown several times in this case was the place where Muslim males were separated to initially. Do you have any recollection of that white house, having seen either it immediately before or after your interview?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learnt of the white house during the course of these proceedings here, during the trial. There are a lot of white houses in that area. Not only in that area, in others too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you continue on through Potocari to get to your destination or did you turn around back and go another way?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I turned back and went back to Bratunac and then to Voljevica, and from Voljevica to Sase, and from Sase to Pribicevac. That is the direction I took previously, and not only I took but everybody else took that direction until the other road had been passable, made passable, the route.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The direction of Bratunac is on the right side of the photograph, and the direction to Potocari is on the left side of the photograph. Now, General, why did you turn around? Why didn't you just go on through the centre of Potocari, on towards Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. McCloskey, excuse me, please. I am trying not to intervene, but I feel I have to at this point. I think that we're going 'round and 'round in circles, because the General has already explained all this. You keep repeating, and we would like to tell you -- and you say that on Wednesday you will be ending the cross-examination. So organise your time well if you wish to do this by Wednesday. What I want to say is that I think that the General has already answered that question that you're asking him now. The answer was that there was a checkpoint which did not allow passage. But at any rate, the General is going to answer the question, but, Mr. McCloskey, please refrain from repetition, otherwise, we're going to waste too much time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. It was my understanding that the checkpoint stopped him, but it was not my understanding that it prevented him from going on further, and if I missed that in the record, I apologise. That was my only question, whether or not he was able to go on further or whether he turned around.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. But having made that precision, go ahead with your question and let's hear what the General has to say. I thought he was saying that the people that were there at the checkpoint told him that only if he had an order from General Mladic was anybody allowed to pass. So that gives me the idea that he had no possibility of continuing. But ask the question and we'll hear it in detail, the answer in detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: General, was the reason that you turned around and went back towards Bratunac because the soldiers at the checkpoint wouldn't let you go through?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so, because they had received orders from General Mladic not to allow anybody to pass through, and this was the order issued. And I came to realise that it would not be good to go on further because I had only two soldiers with me. I just had the two drivers. I had no special security and the situation was unclear, continued to be unclear, and that's why I returned. I went back for those two reasons. The first reason, that I respected what the soldiers told me, and I did an about-turn and went back.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you see General Mladic in the area at any time while you were at this checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Mladic stayed behind me. General Mladic stayed behind me. I didn't know where he was going to go, whether to Potocari or to some other place after the meeting in Bratunac ended.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, the video, I'm told, is now okay. Perhaps we can play it and then end on that note.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is the technical booth ready to play the video?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's being played. Apparently, Your Honour, there's no sound. However, I would like to get out of Potocari, and we have the transcript, so if we can just watch this and we'll be ready to exit the town. I think that may be an appropriate place to stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we play the video, Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The video booth has informed me that it's ready to go with the sound.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We can try again with a little sound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the sound, because we weren't getting any sound. Let's try once again from the beginning now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, finally we were able to see the video. Can we now take a break, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'd appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that this is high time to adjourn, with all these noises going on. There seems to be something amiss. I think that all the teams seem to be tired. Judge Fouad Riad, perhaps your microphone is better than mine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: General Krstic, if you remember what you were saying, you said, "Nothing will stop us." "Stop us" from what?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I meant checking out the terrain which would have to be done and to group the units with respect to the Zepa assignment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We have no further questions for the day. I wish I could say that, Your Honour, for the cross-examination, but we must go on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I think I'll have to stop talking because my microphone is not functioning properly. We resume tomorrow morning at 9.20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
